messages:
neha: Heads-up: Acme Health POC is seeing streaming failures on patient-summary endpoint. Demo is 24h away and this is a blocker. They get SSE disconnects + client JSON.parse errors.
anna: Client provided a short fragment from the browser console:
```
Error: Unexpected end of JSON input
```
And the captured SSE stream fragment:
```
data: {\"id\":\"p-867\",\"name\":\"Ana\",\"summary\":\"Allergies: none\\nMedications: aspirin\"\n\
data: {\"id\":\"p-868\",\"name\":\"Bob\"  <-- truncated here
```
anna: They say it usually fails after 20-40s, often when a larger patient record is emitted.
dmitri: Two immediate suspects: app/server is flushing mid-object (partial JSON sent as multiple SSE events) or an intermediate proxy/LB is terminating the TCP after idle. Also EPIPE on the app usually indicates the remote end closed first.
sam: Which client library are they using? Plain EventSource? Any polyfills?
anna: React app using an EventSource polyfill for older browsers.
sam: Ok. Short-term mitigation for the demo: (1) make each SSE event contain a fully-formed JSON object (don't split a single JSON record across flushes), (2) enable heartbeat comments/pings every 10-15s to keep proxies alive, (3) ask client to buffer and only JSON.parse when full object delim detected.
neha: Can we push a canary with those changes now?
dmitri: Yes. I also want logs: nginx upstream messages, app stdout around the failing request. If we see "upstream prematurely closed connection" it's the app or its runtime throwing.
anna: Proxy log snippet they sent:
```
[2026-03-03T18:12:05Z] GET /v1/stream/patient-summary 200 chunked
[2026-03-03T18:12:33Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.5.6.7, server: api.acme, request: "GET /v1/stream/patient-summary", upstream: "http://10.20.30.40:8080/", host: "api.acme"
```
dmitri: That lines up. App must be closing. Can you get app logs?
anna: App stdout excerpt shows repeated flush logs then an error:
```
streamer: flush 6144 bytes id=p-867
streamer: flush 4096 bytes id=p-867
Error: write EPIPE
    at afterWriteDispatched (internal/stream_base_commons.js:...)
```
sam: EPIPE -> client/proxy closed the connection. So we likely were mid-event when socket closed. Fixing server to send per-event complete JSON avoids client parse hiccups. Also add SSE ":\n" comment heartbeats every 12s.
dmitri: For enterprise customers, proxy idle timeouts and corporate firewalls are common. Recommend heartbeat interval <20s. Also recommend Dedicated capacity for production to reduce intermediates.
neha: Quick client workaround to avoid parse exceptions?
sam: Buffer SSE data on client and only parse when you detect full object boundary. Example pattern for EventSource (pseudo):
```
let buf = '';
es.addEventListener('message', e => {
  buf += e.data;
  try {
    const obj = JSON.parse(buf);
    handle(obj);
    buf = '';
  } catch(err) {
    // partial JSON, wait for more
  }
});
```
Also recommend parsing on double-newline delimiter if using ndjson/sep markers.
anna: I've asked the client to try the canary URL where we enabled full-event flush + heartbeat. Deploy bot shows canary deployed.
deploy-bot: canary: deployed rev b7d2 -> streaming: enable_full_event_flush=true, sse_heartbeat_seconds=12 (19:03 UTC)
anna: Client tested the canary and reported: "no parse errors over 2 hours, connection stayed open, events arrive as complete JSON objects"
neha: Good. Does this clear the "streaming reliability" item in the enterprise checklist or do we still have the SEC questions pending?
anna: Acme's security team still needs confirmation on audit log retention and KMS usage for PII. I've looped in SEC. For the demo, streaming reliability is unblocked.
dmitri: Follow-up action items: 1) run a 24h canary soak test and collect reconnection metrics, 2) add an SSE reconnection alert on the platform if >5% clients reconnect within 5m window, 3) create a short doc snippet for customers with SSE best practices (heartbeat, per-event JSON, client buffering).
neha: Thanks all 8515; I'll update the opportunity and mark POC as "ready for demo".
anna: Demo scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT.
deploy-bot: monitor: streaming-canary healthy (no reconnection spikes in last 10m)
